target_customer: Adults living with chronic illness such as fibromyalgia, long Covid and endometriosis, paying via an optional Pro subscription
problem: People with chronic illness struggle to track symptoms, plan energy and give doctors a coherent history, and often wait years for a diagnosis.
business_model: Consumer mobile app with a free tier and an optional Pro subscription for unlimited chats and enhanced memory

founders.name: Marshall Gould
education: MSc Genomic Medicine, University of Oxford
founders.background_notes: YC page: author of 3 scientific publications and multiple hackathon wins; press says he lives with chronic illness.

founders.name: Isaac Tolley
founders.background_notes: Press says he waited 14 years for a diagnosis.

competitors.name: Sana Health
competitors.what: Symptom and pain tracking with AI help understanding health records

competitors.name: Anecdotal AI
competitors.what: AI app for hard to diagnose conditions with paid unlimited access

technical_complexity.rationale: A voice and text assistant on top of general LLMs with symptom logging and report generation is mostly application engineering; trust and safety around health advice is the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: User histories and memory create some lock in, but general assistants and many small symptom apps can imitate the feature set.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: General assistants added health features during 2025 and 2026; no direct effect on Juno evidenced in sources.

market_need_then: About one billion people live with chronic illness per the company; the founders cite long diagnosis delays and company reported figures include 150,000 downloads in eight months (UCL news) and about 70K monthly recurring revenue (reported by an aggregator).

branding.domain_note: Brand site junocompanion.com and app handle juno-chat; the plain juno.com is not used.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.mascot_or_character: Has a mascot per the site, no name found
identity.visual_style: warm and friendly per the site; front end design spec written in Claude Design per a Claude case study
identity.voice_and_tone: warm, friendly, and positioned as not replacing clinical care

branding.brand_signature: Mascot character in a warm friendly app
branding.community_and_virality: App Store rating of 4.8 claimed on its site and a Product Hunt launch on 2026-06-11; the UCL news item covers the company.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly mascot driven consumer brand with reported download growth, but the name is shared with many other companies named Juno and no independent brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Juno is an active Spring 2026 company launched in late 2025 by two UCL alumni with personal experience of chronic illness, and it reports rapid consumer growth. No exit or failure has occurred. Key uncertainties are retention and monetization from a free tier, and competition from large general assistants entering health.
notes: Funding not verified: aggregators list the standard YC deal (500K) and a pre-seed of unstated size dated 2026-06; no outside investors or Form D were found, so no round is recorded. Usage figures conflict across sources (the site says 350k users in one place and 10,000 in another; UCL says 150,000 downloads). Product launch date 2025-09 comes from an app store listing summary and TechRound says October 2025. Competitors are small apps found through one search and may not be the main rivals.
